[RFCS.5.3] A reader must process `SchemaDef` and `Slot` atoms as they
arrive and add the schema to its descriptor pool before continuing.
When the following `FactAssert` arrives, the descriptor must already be
available; if it is not, [RFCS.5.4] applies.

**Atoms in an embedded DSC front count.** When a stream is
self-contained ([RFCS.13]), the leading DSC's `SchemaDef` / `Slot` atoms
populate the pool exactly as the body's do — they are processed as the
embedded program, not skipped ([RFCS.4.1]). A reader must not wait for
a body announcement of a schema the front already described.

This is a permission for the reader, not a licence for the encoder to
omit: the body still announces every schema it uses ([RFCS.5.1]), so a
stripped stream stays readable.
